title: Exercise Training Intensity and Nitrate Supplementation in Post-Menopausal Females on Hormone Therapy
official: Effects of Exercise Intensity and Inorganic Nitrate Supplementation on Vascular Health and Fitness in Post-Menopausal Females Taking Hormone Therapy
summary: This study is examining whether short-term supplementation with inorganic nitrate in the form of beetroot juice can enhance vascular function in postmenopausal females taking hormone therapy compared to placebo.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

\-- Willingness and ability to comply with schedules and study procedures

* Postmenopausal females aged 45-75, defined as having not had a menstrual cycle for at least 1 year
* BMI \<35 kg/m2
* Currently taking hormone replacement therapy with transdermal estrogen (spray/gel/patches) combined with progesterone for at least 3 months
* MHT regimen started within 10 years of last menses
* MHT regimen started before the age of 60
* Physically inactive (less than 3 bouts of moderate exercise per week or less than a total of 150 minutes per week \[i.e. walking at a brisk pace 3x a week for 50 minutes, leisure sport activity 3x a week for 50 minutes)
* No major changes in medication in the last 3 months

Exclusion Criteria:

* Smokers within the last 5 years
* Weight unstable (loss/gain of more than 3kg in the past 3 months) or currently taking weight loss medications
* Any medical condition that prevents the subject from exercising safely
* Diabetes
* Currently or recently on the following medications (i.e., organic and inorganic nitrates, diuretics, proton pump inhibitors, xanthine oxidase inhibitors etc.)
* Oral antibiotic use now or within the previous four weeks
* Diagnosed with Oral disease or poor oral health
* Using an antibacterial mouthwash or a mouthwash containing chlorhexidine and unwilling to discontinue use
* Cancer diagnosis
* Cardiovascular disease
* Hysterectomy or oophorectomy
* Prisoners, cognitively impaired individuals, and non-English speaking individuals
